question: Should `socket.drain` be accepted as a public read-scoped Gateway teardown event that may close slow subscribers, or should this PR preserve current slow-consumer behavior while documenting the event contract first?
rationale: The branch mixes a useful routing fix with a compatibility-sensitive change to Gateway backpressure semantics, and automation should not choose that public event behavior for maintainers.

options.title: Preserve compatibility before merge
options.body: Require the branch to remove duplicate helpers, keep existing slow-consumer behavior unless explicitly changed, and complete docs/SDK/tests for `socket.drain` before merge.

options.title: Accept close-on-drain semantics
options.body: Merge only after Gateway owners explicitly decide teardown drains should close slow clients and add tests/docs naming that behavior.

options.title: Pause the public event
options.body: Pause or close this PR if `socket.drain` should not become a public Gateway event in its current form.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility before merge
recommendation.body: Require the branch to remove duplicate helpers, keep existing slow-consumer behavior unless explicitly changed, and complete docs/SDK/tests for `socket.drain` before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway/session API work and adjacent broadcast surfaces make this the best available owner for the public event and upgrade-risk decision.
